overview: The Cooper Companies is a global medical device company operating through two segments: CooperVision, a top-three global maker of soft contact lenses (spherical, toric, multifocal, and myopia-management lenses), and CooperSurgical, which supplies women's health and fertility products including IUDs, fertility consumables/equipment, genomic testing, and cryostorage services. The company is headquartered in San Ramon, California, has an October fiscal year-end, and generates revenue globally across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

business_model.summary: CooperVision generates largely recurring revenue from disposable/replacement contact lenses sold through distributors, optometrists, and retail channels, with myopia-management lenses (MiSight) as a high-growth premium sub-segment. CooperSurgical earns revenue from a mix of recurring consumables (IUDs, fertility media) and higher-growth genomics/lab-services and fertility equipment, sold to hospitals, fertility clinics, and clinicians.

revenue_streams.name: CooperSurgical - Office & Surgical / IUDs (incl. Paragard)
revenue_streams.trend: mixed (litigation and new competitor headwinds on Paragard)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2B2C - distributors, group purchasing organizations, independent eye care practices, corporate optical retailers, hospitals, fertility clinics, and authorized resellers
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific; CooperVision has meaningful China exposure (myopia management), CooperSurgical is more US/Europe weighted

main_competitors: Various fertility/IVF equipment and genomics competitors (Vitrolife, Illumina-based genomic testing rivals)
competitive_position.market_position: CooperVision is a top-three global soft contact lens maker with an estimated low-to-mid-20s percent share of the soft lens market, trailing Johnson & Johnson Vision and Alcon but ahead of Bausch + Lomb in most regions; an early leader in myopia management via MiSight, a double-digit-growth clinical niche. CooperSurgical holds a leading position in IUDs (Paragard is the only hormone-free IUD in the US) and a growing presence in fertility genomics/lab platforms.

moat_factors.description: MiSight's FDA and international regulatory approvals as a clinically proven myopia-control lens create a multi-year head start versus new entrants; Paragard is the sole FDA-approved non-hormonal IUD in the US, though a new competitor has now entered.
Contact lens fitting and reordering habits, plus long-standing relationships with eye care professionals and fertility clinicians, create moderate stickiness.
Global manufacturing footprint (UK, Puerto Rico, Hungary, US) supports cost efficiency in a largely commoditized disposable lens category.
MiSight's clinical data and multi-year real-world evidence base support premium positioning in myopia management.

weaknesses: Contact lens category is competitively intense with larger, more diversified rivals (J&J, Alcon) that can outspend on R&D and marketing
Paragard now faces its first non-hormonal IUD competitor in years, eroding a historical monopoly position
CooperSurgical is a collection of smaller, more fragmented businesses with less scale than dedicated women's health/fertility pure-plays
Exposure to litigation risk (Paragard) that is difficult to predict and has already required settlement/reserve actions

growth_drivers: Myopia management (MiSight) expansion - 20% organic growth in Q3 FY2026, new market launches (UK/Europe MyDay MiSight, Japan approval in 2025) and expanding penetration in a still-underpenetrated global category
CooperVision sales force expansion targeting 5,000 additional points of distribution ('doors') in the US
Accelerated R&D pipeline - management has pulled forward product launches previously slated for as far out as 2030
Fertility segment growth via genomic testing and laboratory management platform adoption (fertility revenue +5% in Q3 FY2026)
Capital return - expanded buyback authorization (~$1.5B remaining) following completion of the strategic review
Long-term secular tailwinds: rising global myopia prevalence (especially Asia), growing fertility treatment access and government support for IVF/fertility benefits

business.description: More than 140 direct lawsuits and 4,000+ cases pending in the federal MDL as of mid-2026; management has concluded a loss is probable and reasonably estimable, with potential exposure exceeding available insurance coverage. Bellwether trials ongoing (next trial Sept 28, 2026) will help shape settlement ranges.

business.risk: New competitive entrant in non-hormonal IUD market
business.description: Loss of Paragard's historical monopoly position in the non-hormonal IUD category pressures CooperSurgical revenue/margin and was cited as a factor depressing its standalone valuation during the strategic review.

business.risk: US contact lens channel inventory dynamics
business.description: CooperVision proactively reduced US channel inventory in Q3 FY2026, masking underlying mid-single-digit consumption growth but creating near-term reported revenue softness.
MiSight growth in China lagged EMEA/Americas in recent quarters amid broader China consumer and healthcare-spending softness.
Larger, more diversified competitors (J&J Vision, Alcon) can outspend Cooper on innovation and marketing across contact lenses.

financial.description: Significant international manufacturing (UK, Hungary) and sales footprint create FX translation/transaction headwinds; management flagged continued FX pressure into Q4 FY2026.

Management guided to an increase in the effective tax rate to roughly 17.5% in fiscal 2027, and Q3 FY2026 GAAP results were skewed by a one-time $307.2M discrete tax benefit from a UK tax examination that will not recur.
Debt/equity of ~0.34x and net debt/EBITDA of ~2.8x (per latest screen) is moderate but not immaterial, particularly if litigation reserves or a large settlement require additional financing.

regulatory.description: Contact lenses, IUDs, and fertility devices are regulated medical products subject to FDA and international approval processes; new product launches (myopia lenses, IUDs) require regulatory clearance in each market.
The Paragard litigation illustrates ongoing mass-tort risk inherent to implantable/insertable medical devices.

macro.description: Contact lenses are semi-discretionary; fertility treatments are often self-pay or partially insured and sensitive to consumer confidence and employer benefit trends.
Moderate leverage means higher-for-longer rates raise interest expense and refinancing costs.
Management noted lower tariff refunds expected in Q4 FY2026, indicating tariff policy is already a modest margin factor for the global manufacturing/distribution network.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global soft contact lens market growing mid-single-digits with myopia management as a structurally faster-growing (double-digit) sub-segment driven by rising global myopia prevalence, especially in Asia; fertility/IVF market benefiting from expanding access, employer benefits, and government support in several countries.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate - contact lenses are a recurring, replenishment-driven category with some discretionary elasticity; fertility and elective women's health procedures carry more cyclicality tied to consumer confidence and insurance/benefit coverage.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate - moderate leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~2.8x) means rate moves affect interest expense but the business is not capital-intensive relative to revenue.
key_input_costs: Currency (GBP, EUR, HUF exposure against USD reporting)

recent_developments.event: Q3 FY2026 results: revenue $1.066B (+1% YoY, 1% organic); non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.15 (+4% YoY); GAAP EPS $2.24 boosted by a one-time $307.2M UK tax benefit; record quarterly free cash flow of $273.0M (+66% YoY).

Completed strategic review (initiated December 2025): Board unanimously decided to retain CooperSurgical rather than sell it, citing temporary valuation pressure from a new non-hormonal IUD competitor and the fertility litigation settlement; expanded share buyback authorization by $1B to ~$1.5B remaining capacity.
Reports emerged that Cooper was preparing to divest CooperSurgical, with Wells Fargo estimating a potential deal value near $4.1B; process ultimately concluded without a sale.

CooperVision proactively reduced US channel inventory, holding headline revenue growth to flat while underlying consumption grew mid-single-digits; management is expanding sales coverage by 5,000 doors and accelerating R&D, pulling forward product launches previously planned for as late as 2030.
MiSight (myopia management) delivered 20% organic growth with double-digit gains in EMEA and the Americas, though China remained soft.

Paragard IUD litigation escalated: over 140 direct lawsuits and 1,500+ proffered claimants as of June 2026, more than 4,000 cases pending in the federal MDL; management concluded a loss is probable and reasonably estimable; defendants won the first bellwether trial, with the next trial scheduled September 28, 2026.
CooperVision received approval from Japan's health ministry for MiSight 1-day, the first soft contact lens authorized in Japan for pediatric myopia control.
CooperVision launched MyDay MiSight 1-day in the UK and select European markets, broadening its myopia-management lens portfolio.

items.notes: Full-year guidance range provided alongside Q3 results.
Sequential guidance issued with Q3 results.
Reflects continued fertility (genomics/lab platform) strength offset by IUD competitive/litigation pressure.
Guidance excludes one-time items such as the Q3 UK tax benefit.
Management flagged a higher tax rate for FY2027 versus FY2026, partly reflecting the non-recurrence of the UK discrete tax benefit.
Announced concurrently with completion of the strategic review as a signal of capital-return commitment after deciding not to sell CooperSurgical.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Al White said the Board concluded 'shareholders are better served by continued ownership than pursuing a transaction' for CooperSurgical, attributing depressed sale valuations to temporary factors (new non-hormonal IUD competitor, fertility litigation settlement) rather than structural business deterioration. Management emphasized underlying CooperVision consumption strength (mid-single-digit) masked by deliberate channel inventory reduction, continued momentum in myopia management (MiSight +20% organic), and record free cash flow generation supporting an expanded buyback. Management also flagged FX headwinds, lower Q4 tariff refunds, and a step-up in the FY2027 effective tax rate to ~17.5% as near-term margin considerations.

bull_case: Myopia management (MiSight) is a structurally high-growth, clinically differentiated franchise with a multi-year head start and still-low global penetration, particularly as more Asian and European markets approve/adopt myopia-control lenses
Record free cash flow generation ($273M in Q3 FY2026 alone) and an expanded ~$1.5B buyback authorization support EPS growth and capital return independent of top-line acceleration
Underlying CooperVision consumption trends (mid-single-digit) are healthier than reported revenue suggests once the deliberate US channel inventory reduction laps

Board's decision to retain CooperSurgical, rather than sell into a temporarily depressed valuation, preserves optionality for shareholders if fertility/genomics growth and IUD market conditions normalize

Fertility genomics and lab-management platform revenue is compounding at a healthy clip (+5% organic in Q3 FY2026), diversifying CooperSurgical away from single-product (Paragard) litigation risk over time
bear_case: Paragard litigation is a large, difficult-to-quantify tail risk - management has already concluded a loss is probable and reasonably estimable, with exposure potentially exceeding insurance coverage, and thousands of cases remain pending in the federal MDL
Loss of Paragard's historical monopoly to a new non-hormonal IUD competitor introduces genuine competitive erosion to a previously defensible product line, not just a temporary valuation issue

CooperVision revenue growth has been anemic (flat to +1% reported) for multiple quarters, and it remains uncertain how much of the shortfall is timing (channel destocking) versus genuine share loss to J&J Vision and Alcon
China myopia management softness raises questions about the durability of MiSight's growth trajectory in one of its largest addressable markets

The reversed strategic review (announcing a review, market speculation of a ~$4.1B CooperSurgical sale, then retaining the unit) creates execution and credibility risk, and FY2027 tax-rate step-up plus FX/tariff headwinds pressure near-term EPS comparability
